introduction: Temporary Assistance for Families in Idaho provides qualifying families with cash support. DHW also describes a caretaker-relative grant and possible one-time diversion assistance for particular circumstances.
description: Temporary Assistance for Families in Idaho provides qualifying families with cash support. DHW also describes a caretaker-relative grant and possible one-time diversion assist

sections.who: DHW reviews income, resources, identity and status requirements. Ordinary family assistance and a caretaker-relative grant have different assessments; the relative grant may depend on the child’s finances rather than the adult’s.
sections.get: TAFI is cash assistance for essentials. Eligible families may use direct deposit or an EBT-style card. Employment and training or child-support cooperation may be part of the case.
sections.docs:
• Identification and household income records.
  • Available status and resource information requested by DHW.
  • For a caretaker grant, records showing the relationship and the child’s circumstances.
sections.apply:
1. Start a TAFI application

    Use the options on DHW’s TAFI application page. It lists phone intake at 877-456-1233 and downloaded forms submitted by mail, email or fax.

  2. Explain the type of assistance needed

    State whether you are applying as a family, caring for a relative’s child or facing a circumstance that may fit diversion assistance.

  3. Complete the review

    Provide requested evidence and discuss any employment, training or child-support participation instructions.
sections.after: Read the eligibility and participation notices. Ask DHW to explain how changes in income, household members or caregiving should be reported.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using TAFI application and family/caretaker routes, TAFI benefit and participation overview. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: TAFI provides cash; SNAP is a separate food-assistance program with its own assessment.
Is there help for relative caregivers?
DHW describes a caretaker-relative grant after assessing the relationship and relevant child eligibility.
Can there be a one-time payment?
The agency describes possible diversion assistance for unique circumstances; ask whether your situation fits.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
